Happy belated feast day to our Brother Irenaeus Ceballos, O.S.B., and to his heavenly patron, St. Irenaeus! This year the feast fell on a Sunday, so it was overshadowed by the Lord's Day — but we didn't want to let it pass without honoring him.

St. Irenaeus was the bishop of Lyon, an apologist, and one of the leading Christian theologians of the 2nd century. He defended the faith against the Gnostics and other heretics, and helped establish the canon of the four Gospels. He is the patron of apologists and theologians, and a model of orthodoxy and unity.

Our Brother Irenaeus Ceballos, O.S.B., is a native of Buenos Aires, Colombia, who has lived in the United States for over 29 years and became a U.S. citizen on November 15, 2015. He holds a bachelor's degree in Philosophy from St. John Vianney College in Miami, and spent time as a seminarian for the Palm Beach Diocese, followed by two and a half years at St. Leo Abbey. He entered the postulancy at St. Bernard Abbey in January 2013 and professed his vows as a Benedictine on February 12, 2014. Since then, he has served diligently in groundskeeping and maintenance, contributing to the abbey through painting, general upkeep, and campus maintenance.

Let us pray for St. Irenaeus' intercession to bless Brother Irenaeus and all of us, guiding us in faith and unity.

Yesterday was the feast day of Fr. Joel Martin. Fr. Joel is a native of Fitzgerald, Georgia where he attended public schools, then graduated from Emory University in 1972. After earning M.A. and M.Div. degrees from St. Meinrad School of Theology he taught at St. Bernard Prep from 1991-1995. Then he was made Headmaster of the School and served in that position over fifteen years, and then President in 2013. He also serves as a Vocation Director and Choirmaster of St. Bernard Abbey. 

Fr. Joel shares his name with the prophet Joel, who lived in Judah around the 9th century BC and wrote the book of Joel in the Bible. The prophet Joel warned the people of Judah about a coming locust plague and a day of judgment, but also promised God’s mercy and restoration for those who repent and call on his name. The prophet Joel also foretold the outpouring of the Holy Spirit on all people, which was fulfilled on the day of Pentecost.
Let us thank God for the gift of Fr. Joel Martin and the prophet Joel, and ask for their intercession for our community and our world. May they inspire us to seek God and glorify him in all things.

Today we celebrate our beloved Br. Christopher on his feast day, honoring his patron, St. Christopher.

Revered as the patron saint of travelers and motorists, St. Christopher’s intercession is sought for protection along life’s journeys. Legend tells us he once carried a child across a raging river, only to discover the child was Christ himself. St. Christopher's name, meaning "Christ-bearer," serves as a constant reminder for us to carry Christ to others through our daily actions and words.

Br. Christopher embodies this spirit in all he does. Whether welcoming visitors as our Guestmaster or quietly offering a helping hand, a warm smile, and a bit of good humor around the monastery, he serves our community with dedication. He is truly a Christ-bearer for us all.

May Br. Christopher continue to joyfully persevere in his vocation as a Benedictine monk. And through the intercession of St. Christopher, may God grant safety to all travelers—especially those seeking peace, prayer, and hospitality at our abbey.
We are pleased to announce the election of The Right Reverend Brendan J. Seipel, O.S.B., 11th Abbot of St. Bernard Abbey. More information will follow.

On 29 July 2026, bells rang out over the St. Bernard campus to announce the election of the Right Reverend Brendan John Seipel, O.S.B., as the Abbot of Saint Bernard Abbey in Cullman, Alabama. Abbot Brendan becomes the eleventh Abbot in St. Bernard’s 135-year history.

The election process began on 15 June 2026, when the monks gathered in the Abbey Church to celebrate the Mass of the Holy Spirit, invoking the Paraclete’s wisdom and guidance throughout the election process. The Right Rev. Jonathan R. Licari, O.S.B., Abbot President of the American-Cassinese Congregation of Benedictine Monks, was the principal celebrant for the Mass and presided at the election, in which the monks in solemn vows took part. After temporarily recessing the election chapter until canonical recourse could be made to the Holy See, Abbot Jonathan reopened the election chapter on 29 July, when Abbot Brendan was formally elected and confirmed as Abbot.

Immediately following the election chapter, the monks gathered for a service of thanksgiving in the Abbey Church, at which Abbot Brendan presided. Joining the monks were the Most Rev. Steven J. Raica, Bishop of the Diocese of Birmingham in Alabama, the Most Rev. Robert J. Baker, Bishop Emeritus of the Diocese of Birmingham, priests of the Diocese, Benedictine Sisters of Sacred Heart Monastery, and lay faithful who came to give thanks to God.

Abbot Brendan assumes responsibility as spiritual and temporal leader of St. Bernard immediately; as is customary, the formal blessing of the new Abbot will take place in the coming months.

Abbot Brendan, a native of Lanesville, Indiana, entered St. Bernard Abbey in 2002 and professed vows as a Benedictine monk on 21 March 2004. Over the years, he has served as Guest Master, Director of the St. Boniface Retreat Center, Director of the Abbey Farm, a member of the Senior Council, and as Subprior and Prior.

Here at St. Bernard, Father Dominic carries on that same blend of intellectual rigour and spiritual devotion. We are abundantly blessed by his priesthood, leadership, and service. Please join us in praying for Father Dominic as he steps into his new duties as Prior and continues his vital work in our school.

Yesterday we celebrated the feast day of St. Augustine, patron saint of our Br. Augustine! A newly professed monk and former Navy submariner, Br. Augustine serves as Webmaster. As the son of an Air Force officer, he was born in Pittsburgh, PA, and grew up in Dayton, OH, San Angelo, TX, Azores, Portugal, and Wichita Falls, TX. He has also lived in Hungary, Spain, and Hawaii.

St. Augustine was one of the greatest Christian thinkers and writers of all time. He was born in 354 in Algeria and converted to Christianity after a long and restless search for truth. He became the bishop of Hippo and wrote many influential works, such as Confessions and The City of God. He is also known for his doctrines of original sin, grace, and predestination. He died in 430 during the siege of Hippo by the Vandals. St. Augustine’s life and writings inspire us to seek God with all our heart, mind, and soul, and to love our neighbor as ourselves. He is the patron saint of brewers, printers, theologians, sore eyes, and many cities around the world. Let us ask for his intercession today and always.
St. Augustine, pray for us!

Today is the feast day of Pope St. Linus, the second bishop of Rome and a martyr of the early church. He is mentioned in the New Testament by St. Paul in 2 Timothy 4:21. He was entrusted with the office of the episcopate by the apostles Peter and Paul, and he ruled the church from about 67 to 76 or 79. He is among the martyrs named in the canon of the mass and his relics are venerated in several churches.

We ask for the intercession of Pope St. Linus, who followed Christ faithfully and served his church with love and dedication. May he inspire us to live out our baptismal call to holiness and mission. We also thank God for the gift of Fr. Linus, who enriches our community with his talents and his joy. Happy feast day!

Today, we celebrate the Feast of the Holy Archangels—Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael—who are God’s faithful messengers, powerful protectors, and healers. On this joyful feast day, we celebrate with gratitude two of our own brothers who carry the names of these heavenly patrons: Br. Michael Gregerson, O.S.B. and Br. Raphael Ray, O.S.B.

A native of the vibrant city of New Orleans, Louisiana, Br. Michael served his country in the Air Force with courage and fidelity before answering the call to monastic life. For many years, he served our community as our dedicated sacristan, faithfully caring for the sacred vessels and vestments that adorn our daily liturgy.

Hailing from Lebanon, Tennessee, Br. Raphael shares his energy and guidance with the youth of our school, teaching Civics and Physical Education at St. Bernard Prep. Having recently professed his simple vows, Br. Raphael is currently continuing his formation in the Juniorate. We ask for your special prayers for him today as he continues to dive deeper into the Rule of St. Benedict, that he may persevere with joy toward his solemn vows.

The archangels are honored in Sacred Scripture and tradition as special agents of God’s plan of salvation—announcing His word, defending His people, and healing His creation. As our guardians and intercessors, they accompany us on our earthly pilgrimage toward our heavenly home.

Let us invoke their names today with confidence and thanksgiving, especially for Br. Michael and Br. Raphael:

St. Michael, defend us in battle.

St. Gabriel, announce to us God’s will.

St. Raphael, heal us from all ills.

Holy archangels, pray for us, for our brothers, and for the whole world. Amen.

On Sept. 29, 1891, a significant chapter in St. Bernard’s history began.
A solemn Pontifical Mass was celebrated by Bishop Leo Haid, O.S.B., D.D., at 8 a.m., Father Dennis acting as archpriest, Father Benedict as deacon and Father Fridolin as subdeacon.

The election for the first abbot of St. Bernard took place in the sacristy at 9:30 a.m. and was concluded quickly, since Father Benedict Menges was chosen unanimously as the first abbot on the first ballot.

The loud ringing of the bells brought the good news to the people of Cullman. Once the Te Deum had been sung, the people who had gathered in the churchyard were given the election results and presented with their newly elected abbot. That night, a brass band played for him, and a telegram was sent with news of the election to St. Vincent and the other abbeys.

One hundred thirty-five years have now passed, and we recall the establishment of St. Bernard and the event that marked the start of its history in Cullman.

Happy Founding Day, St. Bernard! 🎉
